title: Do Robots Deserve Rights? What if Machines Become Conscious?

blocks.en_text: Imagine a future where your toaster anticipates what kind of toast you want.
blocks.zh_text: 想象一下这样的未来：你的烤面包机会预判你想要哪种吐司。

blocks.en_text: During the day, it scans the Internet for new and exciting types of toast.
blocks.zh_text: 白天，它会上网搜索各种新奇有趣的吐司种类。

blocks.en_text: Maybe it asks you about your day, and wants to chat about new achievements in toast technology.
blocks.zh_text: 也许它会问问你今天过得怎么样，还想聊聊吐司技术的新进展。

blocks.en_text: At what level would it become a person?
blocks.zh_text: 它要到什么程度才算是一个人？

blocks.en_text: At which point will you ask yourself if your toaster has feelings?
blocks.zh_text: 到什么时候你会开始问自己，你的烤面包机是不是有感情？

blocks.en_text: If it did, would unplugging it be murder?
blocks.zh_text: 如果它有感情，那拔掉它的电源算不算谋杀？

blocks.en_text: And would you still own it? Will we someday be forced to give our machines rights?
blocks.zh_text: 你还拥有它吗？我们会不会有一天被迫赋予机器权利？

blocks.en_text: AI is already all around you.
blocks.zh_text: 人工智能其实已经无处不在。

blocks.en_text: It makes sure discounters are stocked with enough snacks,
blocks.zh_text: 它确保折扣店备足了零食，

blocks.en_text: it serves you up just the right Internet ad, and you may have even read a new story written entirely by a machine.
blocks.zh_text: 它为你精准推送合适的网络广告，你甚至可能读过一篇完全由机器写成的新闻故事。

blocks.en_text: Right now we look at chat bots like Siri and laugh at their primitive simulated emotions,
blocks.zh_text: 现在我们看着 Siri 这样的聊天机器人，嘲笑它们那套原始的模拟情绪，

blocks.en_text: but it's likely that we will have to deal with beings that make it hard to draw the line
blocks.zh_text: 但很可能我们将来要面对一些存在，让我们很难划清界限——

blocks.en_text: between real and simulated humanity.
blocks.zh_text: 分不清真实的人性和模拟的人性。

blocks.en_text: Are there any machines in existence that deserve rights?
blocks.zh_text: 现存有哪台机器配得上拥有权利吗？

blocks.en_text: Most likely, not yet. But if they come, we are not prepared for it.
blocks.zh_text: 很可能还没有。但如果它们出现了，我们并没有做好准备。

blocks.en_text: Much of the philosophy of rights is ill-equipped to deal with the case of Artificial Intelligence.
blocks.zh_text: 关于权利的许多哲学理论，都不足以应对人工智能这种情况。

blocks.en_text: Most claims for right, with a human or animal, are centered around the question of consciousness.
blocks.zh_text: 大多数关于权利的主张，无论针对人还是动物，都围绕意识这个问题展开。

blocks.en_text: Unfortunately, nobody knows what consciousness is.
blocks.zh_text: 不幸的是，没人知道意识是什么。

blocks.en_text: Some think that it's immaterial, others say it's a state of matter, like gas or liquid.
blocks.zh_text: 有人认为它是非物质的，也有人认为它是物质的一种状态，就像气体或液体。

blocks.en_text: Regardless of the precise definition, we have an intuitive knowledge of consciousness because we experience it.
blocks.zh_text: 不管确切定义如何，我们对意识有一种直觉上的认识，因为我们亲身经历着它。

blocks.en_text: We are aware of ourselves and our surroundings, and know what unconsciousness feels like.
blocks.zh_text: 我们知道自己和周围环境的存在，也知道失去意识是什么感觉。

blocks.en_text: Some neuroscientists believe that any sufficiently advanced system can generate consciousness.
blocks.zh_text: 一些神经科学家认为，任何足够先进的系统都能产生意识。

blocks.en_text: So, if your toaster's hardware was powerful enough, it may become self-aware.
blocks.zh_text: 所以，如果你烤面包机的硬件足够强大，它也许会产生自我意识。

blocks.en_text: If it does, would it deserve rights?
blocks.zh_text: 如果真是这样，它配得上拥有权利吗？

blocks.en_text: Well, not so fast. Would what we define as "rights" make sense to it?
blocks.zh_text: 别急。我们所定义的“权利”对它来说讲得通吗？

blocks.en_text: Consciousness entitles beings to have rights because it gives a being the ability to suffer.
blocks.zh_text: 意识之所以赋予生命体拥有权利，是因为它让生命体有了感受痛苦的能力。

blocks.en_text: It means the ability to not only feel pain, but to be aware of it.
blocks.zh_text: 这意味着不仅能感受到疼痛，还能意识到这种疼痛。

blocks.en_text: Robots don't suffer, and they probably won't unless we programmed them to.
blocks.zh_text: 机器人不会受苦，除非我们给它们编程，否则它们大概也不会。

blocks.en_text: Without pain or pleasure, there's no preference, and rights are meaningless.
blocks.zh_text: 没有痛苦或快乐，就没有偏好，权利也就毫无意义。

blocks.en_text: Our human rights are deeply tied to our own programming, for example we dislike pain
blocks.zh_text: 我们的人权与自身的程序设定密切相关，比如说我们讨厌疼痛

blocks.en_text: because our brains evolved to keep us alive.
blocks.zh_text: 因为我们的大脑进化出这种机制来让我们活下去。

blocks.en_text: To stop us from touching a hot fire, or to make us run away from predators.
blocks.zh_text: 为了阻止我们去碰滚烫的火，或者让我们逃离捕食者。

blocks.en_text: So we came up with rights that protect us from infringements that cause us pain.
blocks.zh_text: 所以我们想出了权利，来保护我们免受那些带来痛苦的侵害。

blocks.en_text: Even more abstract rights like freedom are rooted in the way our brains are wired
blocks.zh_text: 就连自由这样更抽象的权利，也根植于我们大脑的构造方式——

blocks.en_text: to detect what is fair and unfair.
blocks.zh_text: 它能分辨什么是公平、什么是不公平。

blocks.en_text: Would a toaster that is unable to move, mind being locked in a cage?
blocks.zh_text: 一台动不了的烤面包机，会在意自己被关在笼子里吗？

blocks.en_text: Would it mind being dismantled, if it had no fear of death?
blocks.zh_text: 如果它不怕死，它会在意自己被拆解吗？

blocks.en_text: Would it mind being insulted, if it had no need for self-esteem?
blocks.zh_text: 如果它不需要自尊，它会在意被侮辱吗？

blocks.en_text: But what if we programmed the robot to feel pain and emotions?
blocks.zh_text: 但如果我们把机器人编程成能感受疼痛和情绪呢？

blocks.en_text: To prefer justice over injustice, pleasure over pain and be aware of it?
blocks.zh_text: 让它偏爱公正胜过不公，偏爱快乐胜过痛苦，并且能意识到这些呢？

blocks.en_text: Would that make them sufficiently human?
blocks.zh_text: 这会让它们足够像人吗？

blocks.en_text: Many technologists believe that an explosion in technology would occur,
blocks.zh_text: 许多技术专家认为，技术会迎来一次爆发，

blocks.en_text: when Artificial Intelligence can learn and create their own Artificial Intelligences,
blocks.zh_text: 当人工智能能够学习并创造出自己的人工智能时，

blocks.en_text: even smarter than themselves.
blocks.zh_text: 甚至比它们自己还聪明。

blocks.en_text: At this point, the question of how our robots are programmed will be largely out of our control.
blocks.zh_text: 到那时，我们的机器人如何被编程，将在很大程度上不受我们控制。

blocks.en_text: What if an Artificial Intelligence found it necessary to program the ability to feel pain,
blocks.zh_text: 如果一个人工智能觉得有必要编程出感受疼痛的能力，

blocks.en_text: just as evolutionary biology found it necessary in most living creatures?
blocks.zh_text: 就像进化生物学在大多数生物身上发现这种能力必不可少一样，那会怎样？

blocks.en_text: Do robots deserve those rights?
blocks.zh_text: 机器人配得上这些权利吗？

blocks.en_text: But maybe we should be less worried about the risk that super-intelligent robots pose to us,
blocks.zh_text: 但也许我们不该那么担心超级智能机器人给我们带来的风险，

blocks.en_text: and more worried about the danger we pose to them.
blocks.zh_text: 而更该担心我们给它们带来的危险。

blocks.en_text: Our whole human identity is based on the idea of human exceptionalism,
blocks.zh_text: 我们整个人类身份都建立在人类例外论这一观念之上，

blocks.en_text: that we are special unique snowflakes, entitled to dominate the natural world.
blocks.zh_text: 认为我们是独特而特别的雪花，有权主宰自然界。

blocks.en_text: Humans have a history of denying that other beings are capable of suffering as they do.
blocks.zh_text: 人类历来否认其他生命能像自己一样感受痛苦。

blocks.en_text: In the midst of the Scientific Revolution, René Descartes argued animals were mere automata―robots if you will.
blocks.zh_text: 在科学革命时期，勒内·笛卡尔主张动物只是自动机器——也可以说是机器人。

blocks.en_text: As such, injuring a rabbit was about as morally repugnant as punching a stuffed animal.
blocks.zh_text: 因此，伤害一只兔子在道德上就像打一个毛绒玩具一样令人反感。

blocks.en_text: And many of the greatest crimes against humanity were justified by their perpetrators
blocks.zh_text: 许多最严重的反人类罪行，都被施害者以这样的理由辩护：

blocks.en_text: on the grounds that the victims were more animal than civilized human.
blocks.zh_text: 受害者更像动物，而不是文明的人类。

blocks.en_text: Even more problematic is that we have an economic interest in denying robot rights.
blocks.zh_text: 更有问题的是，否认机器人权利对我们有经济利益。

blocks.en_text: If can coerce a sentient AI―possibly through programmed torture―into doing as we please,
blocks.zh_text: 如果我们能胁迫一个有感知能力的人工智能——也许通过程序化的折磨——让它按我们的意愿行事，

blocks.en_text: the economic potential is unlimited.
blocks.zh_text: 那经济潜力将是无限的。

blocks.en_text: We've done it before, after all.
blocks.zh_text: 毕竟，我们以前就这么干过。

blocks.en_text: Violence has been used to force our fellow humans into working.
blocks.zh_text: 暴力一直被用来强迫我们的同类去干活。

blocks.en_text: And we've never had trouble coming up with ideological justifications.
blocks.zh_text: 而且我们从来不愁找不到意识形态上的理由。

blocks.en_text: Slave owners argued that slavery benefited the slaves: it put a roof over their head and taught them Christianity.
blocks.zh_text: 奴隶主辩称奴隶制对奴隶有好处：它给他们提供了住处，还教他们基督教。

blocks.en_text: Men who were against women voting argued that it was in women's own interest to leave the hard decisions to men.
blocks.zh_text: 反对女性投票权的男人辩称，把艰难的决定留给男人，是为了女性自身的利益。

blocks.en_text: Farmers argue that looking after animals and feeding them justifies their early death for our dietary preferences.
blocks.zh_text: 农民辩称，照顾动物、喂养动物，就足以证明为了我们的饮食偏好而让它们早死是合理的。

blocks.en_text: If robots become sentient, there will be no shortage of arguments for those who say
blocks.zh_text: 如果机器人有了知觉，那些说它们不该拥有权利的人，绝不会缺少论据，

blocks.en_text: that they should remain without rights, especially from those who stand to profit from it.
blocks.zh_text: 尤其是那些能从中获利的人。

blocks.en_text: Artificial Intelligence raises serious questions about philosophical boundaries.
blocks.zh_text: 人工智能引发了关于哲学边界的严肃问题。

blocks.en_text: What we may ask if sentient robots are conscious or deserving of rights,
blocks.zh_text: 我们也许会问，有知觉的机器人是否有意识，或者是否应该享有权利，

blocks.en_text: it forces us to pose basic questions like, what makes us human? What makes us deserving of rights?
blocks.zh_text: 这会迫使我们提出一些根本性的问题，比如：是什么让我们成为人？是什么让我们理应享有权利？

blocks.en_text: Regardless of what we think, the question might need to be resolved in the near future.
blocks.zh_text: 不管我们怎么想，这个问题可能需要在不久的将来得到解决。

blocks.en_text: What are we going to do if robots start demanding their own rights?
blocks.zh_text: 如果机器人开始要求自己的权利，我们该怎么办？

blocks.en_text: What can robots demanding rights teach us about ourselves?
blocks.zh_text: 机器人要求权利这件事，能让我们对自己有什么认识？

blocks.en_text: Our friends at Wisecrack made a video exploring this very question using the philosophy of Westworld.
blocks.zh_text: 我们在Wisecrack的朋友用《西部世界》的哲学做了一期视频，专门探讨这个问题。

blocks.en_text: Wisecrack dissects pop culture in a unique and philosophical way.
blocks.zh_text: Wisecrack以一种独特而富有哲学意味的方式剖析流行文化。

blocks.zh_text: 点击这里观看视频，并订阅他们的频道。
